brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: A base with removable bins for small parts
requirements.evidence: Two full hex bbases at (0,0) and (1,0). Bin at (0,0) is a full-depth 3-compartment tray (hex-bin-full-div3) and bin at (1,0) is a full-depth 2-compartment tray (hex-bin-full-div2). Both drop into their cells and are not bolted.

Notch drawer frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) at cell (0,1), set between the two touching bases at (0,0) and (1,0). The configurator offered drawers only as notch frames here, not as a separate drawer part.
Handle (handle:1,0,0;top) with inserts on a top cover at (1,0), offered by the configurator on the cover. Its grip is the top handle, not a separate grab accessory.
Compact two-base unit with a top handle, and the configurator reports no mesh clashes. I cannot verify weight, strength or material; that depends on the material the user chooses for printing.

finish.summary: Built a two-base electronics organizer: full bases at (0,0) and (1,0) with a 3-compartment bin and a 2-compartment bin, a notch drawer frame between them at (0,1), and a top cover with a carry handle over the (1,0) cell. Caps and joint bolts were applied to the open faces; check_build reports no errors and meshClash clear. Caveat: the top cover on (1,0) sits over that cell's bin, so that bin must be lifted out after the cover is removed. Drawer and handle are the configurator's notch frame and cover-top handle; I did not add props, since the brief is about the object itself.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
